t: You're looking at Cromwell Tower, a residential skyscraper in the City of London. It takes its name from Oliver Cromwell, the soldier and statesman widely regarded as one of the most important figures in British history. He rose to prominence as a Parliamentarian commander, was a leading advocate of the execution of Charles I in 1649, and ruled as Lord Protector from December 1653 until his death in September 1658.
